_comment: Backtests over licensed vendor history (packages/backtest). Copy to ~/.cherrypick/config/backtest.json to use it. OFF until 'enabled' is true. Unknown keys are refused, not ignored. The API key is never written here: it lives in the OS keyring under vendor.credential (python -m cherrypick.backtest key set). The vendor's data and every result derived from it stay under the cherrypick home; the licence forbids redistribution and requires the data to be purged within vendor.license.purge_within_days of vendor.license.terminated_on.

vendor._comment: subscription declares what the account can reach (checked against the vendor's own refusals); transport 'python' talks to the vendor directly through its library, 'terminal' through a local Theta Terminal at terminal.host:terminal.port. max_concurrent_requests is the account-wide cap for the tier (Standard: 4).
vendor.name: thetadata

store._comment: dir null = ~/.cherrypick/data/backtest/vendor/<vendor>. cadence_seconds and strikes_each_side match the gex recorder, so a vendor session replays through the same code as a recorded one. request_strike_range is how many strikes each side of the vendor's reference price are FETCHED (wider than kept, so a trend day's moving spot stays inside what was fetched); each sample then keeps the strikes_each_side nearest its own spot, as the recorder does.

windows._comment: Declared once and journaled; never tuned and never chosen by the advisor. The holdout is invisible to every search and is spent once per spec. Sessions from 2026-10-13 are the recorder era, used to validate the vendor data against our own recording.
